newsitem.title: USA: House panel begins review of California race.
newsitem.headline: House panel begins review of California race.

text.p: A three-member House panel Wednesday began an investigation of Democrat Loretta Sanchez's contested victory over Republican incumbent Bob Dornan in California's 46th congressional district last year.

Sanchez won by 979 votes after a recount and her upset victory was certified by the state of California. But Dornan asked the House to overturn the result, alleging that she won because of fraud and ballots cast by non-citizens.

Sanchez was sworn in as a member of Congress Jan. 7, but the House Oversight Committee appointed a task force of two Republicans and one Democrat to investigate Dornan's charges. The full House, which Republicans control, may have to decide the outcome if the panel were to find that Sanchez won by fraud.

Steny Hoyer of Maryland, the panel's only Democrat, asked at the start of the hearing that Dornan's appeal be dismissed, saying Dornan had not proven his charges. But Michigan Republican Vernon Ehlers, the task force chairman, refused. The panel's other member is Ohio Republican Robert Ney.

"It appears to me this matter deserves further investigation. There are very serious allegations of irregularities," Ehlers said. He said he wanted to hold a hearing in Orange County near Los Angeles, where the election took place last November.
"We have to get more information. The way to get more information is to hold a hearing," Ehlers said.
Ehlers said the task force's job was to determine if there was any fraud, illegal voters, miscounting or other irregularities in the election and, if so, whether they affected the outcome.
